cards.name: Rough Pastels
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Artistic filter that redraws the image as strokes of coloured pastel chalk on a textured ground (canvas, burlap, brick or sandstone): in light, bright areas the chalk lies thick with little texture showing, in darker areas the chalk looks scraped thin so the embossed texture comes through. Stroke Length / Stroke Detail set the chalk strokes, Texture / Scaling / Relief / Light Direction set the paper-like ground.
use_for: turning a soft or low-quality photo into a hand-drawn chalk-pastel illustration for a poster or event backdrop
textured, crafty look for a greeting card, menu or book-cover photo
disguising compression blur in a video still by replacing detail with visible strokes
base layer for a mixed-media collage, faded back with Edit/Fade or a smart-filter blend
avoid: Filter > Artistic is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Faces and small type: strokes smear features and lettering; mask the effect off faces and text or keep Stroke Length low.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Very large images: stroke size and texture are in pixels, so on a 4K+ file the effect reads as fine noise; raise Stroke Length and Scaling or work on a downsized copy.

A softer painterly look without chalk or paper texture: use Filter/Artistic/Dry Brush or Filter/Stylize/Oil Paint instead (Underpainting is not an escape from texture: it embosses the same canvas / burlap / brick / sandstone ground).

params.name: strokeLength
params.does: Stroke Length: length of the chalk strokes; longer = more streaky and less detail
params.typical: 6 default; 10-30 for a clearly drawn look

params.name: strokeDetail
params.does: Stroke Detail: how sharply the strokes are etched into the image (higher = crisper, more defined strokes)

params.name: textureType
params.does: Texture: the ground the chalk sits on. The dialog lists Brick, Burlap, Canvas and Sandstone; Blocks / Frosted / Tiny Lens come from the shared textureType enum (the Glass filter's textures) and were not render-tested here

params.name: scaling
params.does: Scaling %: size of the texture pattern

params.name: relief
params.does: Relief: how deeply the texture is embossed; higher = stronger 3D grain

params.name: lightDirection
params.does: Light: direction the light hits the embossed texture from
params.typical: lightDirBottom default; lightDirTopLeft looks most natural

params.name: invertTexture
params.does: Invert: swaps raised and sunken parts of the texture

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("strokeLength"), 30); d.putInteger(s("strokeDetail"), 10); d.putEnumerated(s("textureType"), s("textureType"), s("texTypeCanvas")); d.putInteger(s("scaling"), 150); d.putInteger(s("relief"), 35); d.putEnumerated(s("lightDirection"), s("lightDirection"), s("lightDirTopLeft")); d.putBoolean(s("invertTexture"), false); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("roughPastels"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.cost: light: 177 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; a few seconds at most on a full HD frame, more with high Scaling

review.changes: avoid: the 'softer look without chalk texture' alternative named Filter/Artistic/Underpainting, which embosses the same textured ground; replaced with Filter/Artistic/Dry Brush or Filter/Stylize/Oil Paint. Everything else checked against the batch (keys, defaults, ranges, enums, invoke, smart filter, AI/CDR equivalents) and left as is.

verified.note: Diagonal pastel-chalk strokes over a canvas-textured ground across the whole frame, colours kept and a little more saturated.

cards.name: Smudge Stick
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Artistic filter that softens the image with short diagonal strokes that smudge and smear the darker areas, while lighter areas are brightened and lose detail. The result looks like a soft, smeared pastel or charcoal rubbing with a glowing, blown-out quality in the highlights; Highlight Area and Intensity control how much of the image gets that brightening.
use_for: dreamy, smeared painterly background behind a headline
soft hand-rubbed look for a moody poster or album-art photo
hiding compression artefacts in a video still by smearing them into strokes
high-key glowing painting effect on a light photo (raise Highlight Area)
avoid: Filter > Artistic is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Faces and text that must stay readable: the diagonal smearing blurs features and small type; mask them out.
High Highlight Area plus high Intensity blows light areas to flat white; keep one of them moderate on bright photos.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
A clean soft-focus without strokes: use a blur (Filter/Blur/Smart Blur) instead.

params.name: strokeLength
params.does: Stroke Length: length of the diagonal smudge strokes; longer = more smeared

params.name: highlightArea
params.does: Highlight Area: how much of the lighter tones get brightened and washed out

params.name: intensity
params.does: Intensity: strength of the highlight brightening
params.typical: 10 default; 4-8 when Highlight Area is high

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("strokeLength"), 10); d.putInteger(s("highlightArea"), 10); d.putInteger(s("intensity"), 6); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("smudgeStick"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.cost: light: 300 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; a few seconds at most on a full HD frame

review.changes: none: summary, params, defaults and ranges, demo (all in range), scripting keys/event and AI equivalent match the batch; no real CorelDRAW counterpart exists (Dabble maps to Paint Daubs), so CDR stays out.

verified.note: Light areas are brightened and blown out (photo mean 129 vs 106) while darker areas are smeared with short diagonal strokes; the type and hairlines in the dark band are smudged nearly away.

cards.name: Sponge
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Artistic filter that repaints the image as if dabbed on with a sponge: highly textured, mottled areas of contrasting colour with porous blotches, while the overall shapes stay recognisable. Brush Size sets the size of the sponge marks, Definition how contrasty and defined they are, Smoothness how soft their edges are.
use_for: mottled, sponge-painted texture for a rustic or hand-made poster background
turning a blurry video still into a stylised painting where the missing detail is not missed
textured fill photo for a children's book or craft-themed layout
grungy painted backdrop under bold type
avoid: Filter > Artistic is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.

Skin and portraits: the blotchy texture reads as blemishes on faces; mask faces, or for a cleaner paint look use Filter/Artistic/Dry Brush or Filter/Stylize/Oil Paint (not Watercolor, which breaks faces into dark blotches too).
Small type and fine lines: they break up into speckles.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Very large images: sponge marks are pixel-sized, so on a 4K+ file they look like fine noise; work on a downsized copy.

params.name: brushSize
params.does: Brush Size: size of the sponge marks
params.typical: 2 default; 5-10 for a visible sponge texture

params.name: definition
params.does: Definition: contrast and crispness of the sponge texture; higher = darker, more defined blotches

params.name: smoothness
params.does: Smoothness: softens the edges of the sponge marks; low = rough and grainy, high = smoother blobs

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("brushSize"), 10); d.putInteger(s("definition"), 22); d.putInteger(s("smoothness"), 2); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("sponge"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.cost: light: 340 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; a few seconds at most on a full HD frame

review.changes: avoid: recommended Filter/Artistic/Watercolor as the cleaner paint look for faces, which contradicts the Watercolor card (faces break into dark blotches); now points to Filter/Artistic/Dry Brush or Filter/Stylize/Oil Paint. Rest checked and unchanged.

verified.note: Mottled, porous sponge blotches over the whole frame, colour blocks included, while shapes stay recognisable.

cards.name: Underpainting
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Artistic filter that paints the image onto a textured ground and then paints the final image over it: shapes are softened into broad, slightly muted brush areas and the canvas / burlap / brick / sandstone texture shows through as an embossed grain. Brush Size sets how much detail is painted away, Texture Coverage how much of the texture shows, Texture / Scaling / Relief / Light Direction the ground itself.
use_for: turning a photo into a soft oil-on-canvas painting for a poster, invitation or wall print
giving a blurry video frame a deliberate painted, textured finish
canvas-texture base under other Filter Gallery effects (stack in Filter/Filter Gallery)
classic painted portrait look when kept subtle and masked off the eyes
avoid: Filter > Artistic is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Crisp graphics and small type: high Brush Size smears them into blobs; mask them out or keep Brush Size low.
High Relief over the whole image looks like a cheap embossed print; keep it under about 15 for a painted look.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Texture only, without repainting: use Filter/Texture/Texturizer instead.

params.name: brushSize
params.does: Brush Size: size of the underpainting brush; larger = broader, flatter paint areas and less detail
params.typical: 6 default; 10-25 for a clearly painted look

params.name: textClickPoint
params.does: Texture Coverage (harvested key textClickPoint): how much of the image the texture covers / shows through

params.name: textureType
params.does: Texture: the ground the paint sits on. The dialog lists Brick, Burlap, Canvas and Sandstone; Blocks / Frosted / Tiny Lens come from the shared textureType enum (the Glass filter's textures) and were not render-tested here

params.name: scaling
params.does: Scaling %: size of the texture pattern

params.name: relief
params.does: Relief: how deeply the texture is embossed

params.name: lightDirection
params.does: Light: direction the light hits the embossed texture from

params.name: invertTexture
params.does: Invert: swaps raised and sunken parts of the texture

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("brushSize"), 25); d.putInteger(s("textClickPoint"), 30); d.putEnumerated(s("textureType"), s("textureType"), s("texTypeCanvas")); d.putInteger(s("scaling"), 150); d.putInteger(s("relief"), 12); d.putEnumerated(s("lightDirection"), s("lightDirection"), s("lightDirTop")); d.putBoolean(s("invertTexture"), false); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("underpainting"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.cost: light: 348 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; a few seconds at most on a full HD frame, more with high Scaling

review.changes: none: textClickPoint key, defaults (relief 4, light Top), ranges, enum labels, demo values, scripting and AI/CDR equivalents all match the batch.

verified.note: Shapes softened into broad muted brush areas with canvas grain showing through; the white type is smeared into blobs, as the card warns.

cards.name: Watercolor
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Artistic filter that paints the image in a watercolour style with a medium brush loaded with water and colour: detail is simplified into flat, blotchy washes and, where tones change sharply at edges, the colour is saturated and darkened. The result is noticeably darker and higher-contrast than the original, especially in shadows; Shadow Intensity controls how dark those edges and shadows go.
use_for: quick painted-watercolour treatment of a photo for an invitation, travel poster or blog header
stylising a soft video frame so the lack of detail reads as a painting
illustrative background plate behind type (lighten it afterwards with Edit/Fade or a Curves layer)
avoid: Filter > Artistic is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Dark or low-key photos: the filter darkens and can plug shadows to black; keep Shadow Intensity at 0-1 or brighten the image first.
A real airy, light watercolour with white paper showing: this filter looks heavy and dark; combine it with Edit/Fade, a lighter blend, or paint with watercolour brushes instead.
Faces and small type: features and letters break into dark blotches; mask them out.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.

params.name: brushDetail
params.does: Brush Detail: how much detail the brush keeps; low = loose blotchy washes, high = closer to the photo
params.typical: 9 default; 3-8 for a clearly painted look

params.name: shadingIntensity
params.does: Shadow Intensity: how dark the shadows and tonal edges are painted; high values turn much of the image near-black

params.name: texture
params.does: Texture: amount of paper / wash texture in the colour areas (1-3)

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("brushDetail"), 3); d.putInteger(s("shadingIntensity"), 1); d.putInteger(s("texture"), 3); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("watercolor"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.cost: light: 404 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; a few seconds at most on a full HD frame

review.changes: demo_settings + scripting: shadingIntensity 3 -> 1. The plate is half dark areas and dark-red wood and the card's own avoid says keep Shadow Intensity 0-1 on dark areas; at 3 those areas plug to black while brushDetail 3 + texture 3 already make the washes unmistakable. Rest checked and unchanged.

verified.note: Detail simplified into blotchy washes with dark rims at edges; the frame is clearly darker than the plate (photo mean 84 vs 106).
